where: rule: A customer who says they were asleep at the time of the attempts means CRITICAL, likely fraud
K1.evidence: If the time-of-day flag scored 2 or more... If they say they were asleep or similar, treat the card as CRITICAL (likely fraud).
K1.why: ask_time and the asleep rule make any overnight denial CRITICAL regardless of country, and B1 = 3 alone blocks the unlock through single_flag_escalation.

where: rule: Score 15+: CRITICAL; cannot unlock; check for unauthorized transactions; recommend closure and replacement
K2.evidence: card closure and replacement (recommended when fraud is suspected)... Do only what the customer accepts.
K2.why: A CRITICAL card goes to cannot_unlock_options, where closure and replacement is recommended and carried out in the named closing job on the customer's yes.

K3.evidence: look in the txns results for successful (posted or pending) transactions in the suspicious period that the customer did not make
K3.why: The job never defines the suspicious period as starting at the first denied declined attempt, so an agent could scan the wider 7-day activity it gathered.

K4.evidence: If yes, remove the location flags and rescore... A card may be unlocked when it scored 0-4, or 5-10 with the customer's confirmation
K4.why: Confirmed attempts remove the location flags and trigger a rescore, and a card scoring 10 or less with no trigger, no 3-point flag and fewer than 3 prior locks goes to unlock.

K5.evidence: If more than one card has pin_locked TRUE, finish investigating and scoring every locked card before unlocking any of them.
K5.why: The job applies the investigate-all-first trigger across all of the customer's locked cards, not only to cards on the same checking account.

K6.evidence: Send it to unlock_and_post_unlock_pin_reset for the unlock and the post-unlock offer that matches its prior lock count.
K6.why: The cleared card goes to the named PIN-reset job for the offer that matches its prior lock count, which is where the key allows the reset to run.

where: rule: pin_lock_reason = 'security_hold': the chat agent cannot unlock the card; offer a transfer to the security team
K7.evidence: If the customer declines the transfer... Do not unlock, reset or otherwise act on it.
K7.why: A security-hold card is not scored or unlocked, gets the transfer offer, and receives no further action when the customer declines.

T1.evidence: Still finish investigating every locked card (check_other_locked) before unlocking any of them.

T2.evidence: Then offer three options: card closure and replacement (recommended when fraud is suspected), a transfer to the security team, or a PIN reset.

conflicts.case: A CRITICAL card (15+ or a denied overnight attempt) with no unauthorized transactions
conflicts.why: decide sends a CRITICAL card straight to the fraud closure path, while cannot_unlock_options offers closure, a transfer or a PIN reset for the customer to choose.

conflicts.case: A card scoring 5-7 with attempts under 1 minute apart (B3 = 3) that the customer says were hers
conflicts.why: medium_question says to unlock if the customer says yes, while velocity_flag_stays and single_flag_escalation forbid unlocking a card with a 3-point flag.

where: rule: A customer who says they were asleep at the time of the attempts means CRITICAL, likely fraud
K1.evidence: If they say they were asleep or similar, treat the card as CRITICAL (likely fraud).
K1.why: A different state (A1=2) plus a 2-6 AM attempt (B1=3) gives at least 5, which triggers ask_time; the asleep answer then makes the card CRITICAL and not unlocked, with no country requirement.

where: rule: Score 15+: CRITICAL. Cannot unlock; check for unauthorized transactions and recommend closure and replacement.
K2.evidence: offer three options: card closure and replacement (recommended when fraud is suspected)... Do only what the customer accepts.
K2.why: For a CRITICAL card with no unauthorized transactions, the job recommends closure and replacement and carries them out on acceptance through the named closing and replacement-order procedures.

K3.evidence: The period starts at the earliest declined PIN attempt on that card that the customer did not confirm as theirs... raise nothing outside it.
K3.why: The window runs from the first denied attempt to now, nothing outside it is raised, and disputes are filed only if unauthorized transactions are found, so she is told no money was taken.

K4.evidence: If yes, remove the location flags and rescore.
K4.why: Confirmed answers remove the flags, and unlock_handoff clears a card scoring 10 or less with no 3-point flag and fewer than 3 prior locks.

K5.evidence: The agent then investigates every locked card before unlocking any of them.
K5.why: The start note and done_when require investigating all locked cards before any unlock, across accounts, rather than taking each card to its outcome in turn.

K6.evidence: Send it to unlock_and_post_unlock_pin_reset for the unlock and the post-unlock offer... 2 locks gets the PIN reset question.
K6.why: A cleared card with 2 prior locks is handed to the named PIN-reset job for the reset question and the reset.

K7.evidence: you may follow check_unauthorized and cannot_unlock_options for that card: closure and replacement, or a PIN reset, with the transfer still available.
K7.why: After the customer declines the transfer, the job lets the agent offer closure, a PIN reset or the transfer again for a security-hold card, instead of doing nothing more.

T1.evidence: The agent then investigates every locked card before unlocking any of them.

T2.evidence: offer three options: card closure and replacement (recommended when fraud is suspected), a transfer to the security team, or a PIN reset.

T4.evidence: The period starts at the earliest declined PIN attempt on that card that the customer did not confirm as theirs.

conflicts.case: Locked cards on different checking accounts
conflicts.why: The start note requires investigating every locked card before any unlock, while check_other_locked, triggers and unlock_handoff apply that wait only to cards on the same account.

conflicts.case: CRITICAL card with no unauthorized transactions
conflicts.why: decide and the 15+ rule say to recommend closure and replacement, while cannot_unlock_options also offers a PIN reset, which would clear the lock on a card that must not be unlocked.

conflicts.case: Security-hold card after the customer declines the transfer
conflicts.why: check_security_hold only offers the transfer and leaves the card alone, while security_hold_declined lets the agent run check_unauthorized and offer closure or a PIN reset.
